texts.preamble: Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2024 High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:48162 Court No. - 89 Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 40956 of 2023 Applicant :- Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Araf Khan,Lihazur Rahman Khan Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for opposite parties and perused the record.
texts.facts: The rice was seized and given into the custody of one Irshad, the fair price dealer with necessary instructions. The memo was prepared as per law and after taking approval from the District Magistrate the FIR was lodged. The only argument made by the learned counsel for the applicant is that for the offence under Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act, there must be violation of some control order, but in the FIR no control order has been mentioned rather a Government Order has been mentioned. In the absence of violation of any control order the prosecution against the applicant is impermissible. The rice is generally purchased by the applicant from different wholesale godowns before its transportation to the retailer. The purchase bills dated 13.08.2022, 14.08.2022, 15.08.2022 and 17.08.2022 relating to purchase of the rice confiscated in the present case were placed before the court.
texts.arguments: It has been held therein that for prosecution under Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act there must be violation of some notified order/control order. The petitioner was also having IEC issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industries, Department of Commerce. Thus, the only argument of the learned counsel for the applicant on the basis of above judgements is again the same that for invoking the power to lodge an FIR under Section 3/7 of Essential Commodities Act there must be violation of some control order and in the FIR concerned the control order has not been mentioned, the violation of which can be claimed on the part of the applicant. Learned A.G.A., however, opposed the prayer and submitted that in the FIR the Government Order dated 29.07.2003 has been mentioned. He has drawn the attention of the court towards supplementary counter affidavit filed by him mentioning the Uttar Pradesh Essential Commodities (Regulation of Sale and Distribution Control) Order, 2016 and submitted that whereas the State Government is of the opinion that it is necessary and expedient so to do for maintaining the supply of foodgrains and other essential commodities and for securing their equitable distribution and availability on fair price under targeted public distribution system and with this aim the control order dated 29.06.2016 was passed. It is submitted that for the equitable distribution and availability of edibles on fair price, it is necessary that a person dealing in sale and purchase of foodgrains must have the necessary license and registration etc. But neither any license nor any registration has been shown by the applicant to deal with business of sale and purchase of foodgrains. In his written submission learned counsel for the applicant has mentioned that the applicant being the sole proprietor of M/s Bhola Trading Company works in the name and style as above and deals with the transportation of edibles like pulses, rice and pearly millet etc.
